title: Best Daraz Alternative in Pakistan
summary: The best Daraz alternatives in Pakistan compared, for buyers and for sellers: brand stores, social selling, China-direct COD and no-MOQ reselling.
body_markdown:
The best Daraz alternative depends on which half of Daraz you are replacing. It is two businesses in one app: a place to buy, and a place to sell. People search for an alternative from both sides, and the answers have almost nothing in common.


If you are **buying** , you are usually after the same product with fewer counterfeit listings, a return that actually happens, or a price closer to the source. That points you at brand stores, verified local sellers, and China-direct ordering with cash on delivery.


If you are **selling** , you are after the part of every sale that currently leaves your hands: commission, competition on your own listing, and a payment cycle that runs on someone else's calendar. That points you at channels where you own the customer and set your own margin.


Below is each route, honestly, and the one case where nothing beats a big marketplace.


## Why people go looking for a Daraz alternative


Daraz is the default in Pakistan and it earns that position — the reach is real, the app is on most phones, and the logistics network covers cities smaller platforms do not touch. The reasons people leave are specific, not general.


### As a buyer


A large open marketplace lists many sellers against the same product. That is good for price and bad for certainty: two listings for the "same" item can be two different products at two different quality levels. Buyers also get tired of the gap between a listing photo and the box that arrives, and of chasing a return through a seller they cannot reach. None of that is unique to Daraz — it is what happens on any marketplace once it is large enough that sellers compete on price.


### As a seller


The seller complaints are structural. You pay a commission on every sale, the exact rate depending on the category — check the current schedule on Daraz's own seller pages rather than trusting a number in a blog post, including this one. You compete inside the platform against sellers listing the same product, often on price alone. Your money arrives on the platform's payment cycle, not when the customer pays. And the customer is the marketplace's customer, not yours: you cannot message them again, and next month they buy the same thing from whoever is cheapest that day.


If the seller-side maths is what brought you here,[Daraz vs Markaz for resellers](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/daraz-vs-markaz-for-resellers-fees-cod-margins) works through fees, cash-on-delivery risk and margins in detail.


## Decide what you are replacing first


Three different people search this phrase. Find yourself before reading the list.


**You want to buy something.** You need a trustworthy source for one product, at a fair price, that will arrive. Skip to the buyer section.


**You want to sell, and Daraz is taking too much.** You need a channel where the margin stays with you. Skip to the seller section.


**You want to source stock cheaply, then sell it anywhere.** You are not really replacing Daraz — you are replacing a supplier. That is the sourcing question, and it is the last section.


## If you are buying: the alternatives, compared honestly


### 1. Other Pakistani marketplaces


There are smaller general marketplaces and category specialists operating in Pakistan. They are structurally the same product as Daraz — many sellers, one catalogue — which means you inherit the same listing-quality problem in a smaller pool with less competitive pricing. Worth using when a specialist genuinely knows a category; not worth it as a straight swap.


### 2. Brand websites and authorised retailers


For anything where authenticity matters — electronics, cosmetics, supplements, branded fashion — buying from the brand's own Pakistani store or an authorised retailer removes the counterfeit question completely. You usually pay more than the cheapest marketplace listing. For a phone charger, that difference is the whole point.


### 3. Instagram, WhatsApp and Facebook sellers


An enormous share of Pakistani retail runs through social sellers, and the good ones are excellent: you speak to a person, they know their stock, and cash on delivery is standard. The risk is that there is no platform behind them if something goes wrong. Check how long the account has been posting, look for real customer photos rather than stock images, and start with a small order.


### 4. Cross-border shopping apps


The China-based shopping apps put a very large catalogue at prices below local retail. The trade-offs are consistent: card payment rather than cash on delivery, delivery estimates you cannot hold anyone to, duty that may appear after you have paid, and returns that have to cross a border. Fine for a low-value item you are relaxed about. Difficult for anything you need by a specific date.[The best Temu alternative in Pakistan](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/best-temu-alternative-in-pakistan) ranks those routes by what you are actually buying.


### 5. Buying China-direct, in rupees, with cash on delivery


The middle route most people do not know exists: order China products through a Pakistani platform that has already handled freight, duty and clearance, so the price you see is the price you pay, in rupees, with cash on delivery at your door. That is what[Markaz China](https://www.markaz.app/china) does — 10–17 day delivery from China, no card, no customs bill afterwards, no minimum order. Start from[the China categories](https://www.markaz.app/china/categories) if you are browsing rather than hunting a specific item.


### 6. Local markets


For anything you want to see before paying, the city wholesale and retail markets still win on price and on certainty. You inspect the item, you negotiate, you take it home. The cost is your afternoon.


## If you are selling: the alternatives, compared honestly


### 1. Your own store


A Shopify or WooCommerce store makes you the owner of the customer, the pricing and the data. No commission, no competing listings on your own product page. What you take on is traffic — a marketplace hands you buyers, and a store does not. Budget for the fact that your first months are about learning to bring people in, not about the store software.


### 2. Social selling


Selling on Instagram, TikTok, Facebook or a WhatsApp catalogue costs nothing to start and keeps the whole margin. It works because Pakistani buyers already shop this way and trust a seller who answers messages. It is the fastest route from nothing to a first sale, and the least dependent on any platform's fee schedule.


### 3. Reselling landed stock instead of holding your own


The version that removes the capital problem: instead of buying stock and listing it, you sell from a supplier's catalogue and they ship to your customer. You never own inventory, so the money that would have been sitting in cartons stays in your account. On[the Markaz reseller programme](https://www.markaz.app/reseller-pk) there is no minimum order, orders ship cash on delivery, and delivery inside Pakistan runs 3–5 days. Your margin is the difference between the supply price and your selling price, which you set — not a commission rate someone else publishes.


If you already have a website,[the dropshipping portal](https://www.markaz.app/dropshipping-portal) connects the same catalogue to it so the store and the supply side are one system.


### 4. Another marketplace


Listing on a second marketplace is the easiest move and the one that changes the least. You are still renting the customer, still paying a commission, still competing on price inside someone else's search results. Do it for extra reach on top of a channel you control — not as your escape from the first one.


## Where Markaz replaces Daraz — and where it does not


Be clear about what the two things are. Daraz is a marketplace where you list a product and hope a shopper finds it. Markaz is a supply platform: it gives resellers stock at supply prices, in rupees, with no minimum order and cash on delivery, and you sell it wherever your customers already are.


So it replaces Daraz for the seller who wanted margin and control, and it does not replace Daraz for the seller who wanted the marketplace's traffic. If your entire sales engine is "shoppers browsing a marketplace", a supply platform does not hand you that — you bring the customers, and you keep the difference. Most resellers who make the switch already had an audience: a WhatsApp list, an Instagram page, a shop, a neighbourhood.


On the buying side it replaces the cross-border shopping apps rather than Daraz itself, because it solves their specific problem: China prices without a card, without a customs surprise, and without a delivery date nobody will stand behind.[The reseller catalogue](https://www.markaz.app/shop) shows what is already landed in Pakistan;[the category list](https://www.markaz.app/shop/categories) is the faster way in if you know your niche.


## Five checks before you commit to any alternative


1. **Who do you pay, and when?** Cash on delivery and card-before-shipping are different businesses. Know which one you are in before you price anything.
2. **What is the landed price?** If the number on screen does not include getting the item into Pakistan, it is not the price. Add freight, duty and clearance before you compare anything.
3. **What happens on a return?** Ask before you need to know. A return policy you cannot reach across a border is not a return policy.
4. **Can you get the same item again next month?** If you are selling, a source you cannot restock from will cost you a customer at the worst possible moment.
5. **Whose customer is it?** On a marketplace, not yours. On your own channel, yours. That single difference compounds over a year more than any commission rate.


## Which one fits you


**Buying one thing, authenticity matters.** Brand store or authorised retailer. Pay the difference.


**Buying, price matters more than speed.** China-direct with cash on delivery, or a local market if you can get there.


**Selling, and you have no audience yet.** Social selling plus a no-minimum supplier. Learn what people buy before you spend on stock or a store.


**Selling, and you already have an audience.** Move them to a channel you own and source from a supply platform. This is where the commission you were paying turns into margin.


**Selling, and marketplace traffic is your whole business.** Stay on the marketplace. Add a second channel alongside it instead of replacing it.


## Frequently asked questions


### Is there a Pakistani alternative to Daraz for buyers?


Several, but none of them is a like-for-like replacement at the same scale. In practice buyers do not switch to one app — they split: brand stores for anything where authenticity matters, social sellers for fashion and everyday goods, and a China-direct platform when they want the price rather than the speed.


### Is selling on Markaz cheaper than selling on Daraz?


They charge differently, so "cheaper" is the wrong comparison. A marketplace takes a commission on a sale it helped you make. A supply platform sells you stock at a supply price and you set your own selling price, so your margin is your decision. Which comes out ahead depends on whether you can bring your own customers.[The fee and margin comparison](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/daraz-vs-markaz-for-resellers-fees-cod-margins) goes through it properly.


### Can I use both at the same time?


Yes, and plenty of sellers do. Source stock from a no-minimum supplier, sell it on your own channels for full margin, and keep marketplace listings running for the extra reach. The mistake is treating them as a single decision.


### What is the best alternative if I want China prices?


Order China-direct through a platform that handles the import, or import yourself through 1688 or Alibaba once your volumes justify the work. The comparison for each is in[the AliExpress alternatives](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/best-aliexpress-alternative-in-pakistan) and[the Alibaba alternatives](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/best-alibaba-alternative-in-pakistan) for Pakistan.


### Do I need a company registered to sell online?


Not to make your first sales. Register when your volumes, your tax position or a platform's requirements make it necessary — not as a step that delays your first sale by a month.


### Is there a minimum order to start reselling?


Not on Markaz. You can order a single unit, which is the point for anyone testing products — you find out whether something sells for the cost of one of it, not one carton of it.
